clue.text: Chap returned hymnbook in sack

indicators.note: returned means the word for a chap is sent back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Sid is a man's name, so a chap
a missal is a book of prayers and hymns for the Mass

explanation.surface: A man brings back a hymnbook tucked inside a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid is a stock crossword chap; 'in' only links wordplay to the definition, and 'sack' is the noun for being fired, not a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the sack is to receive a firing, so sack as a noun is a synonym for being fired from a job.

clue.text: Doctor behind plan outlined

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for behind, at the stern

explanation.surface: A doctor stands behind a proposal that has been sketched out.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a rough preliminary version, a plan sketched out before the finished thing.

clue.text: Funny film scene initially complicated with Sky broadcast

indicators.note: initially says take only the first letter of the following word
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic movie scene turns out tangled when the Sky channel shows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S from scene; 'broadcast' rearranges S + COMPLICATED + SKY. Sky is a British satellite TV company, which makes 'broadcast' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick comedy is a genre of knockabout physical humour, the stuff of many funny films.

clue.text: Fashionable attitude, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a stance is a position or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: A trendy viewpoint, offered as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the definition is 'example'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration, a synonym of example.

clue.text: Wise to hang rogue, at last

parts.note: to sag is to hang down limply

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word rogue

explanation.surface: It would be wise, finally, to hang the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives E, the final letter of rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage as an adjective means wise and discerning.

clue.text: Puppies, say, left out — here's one making a mess

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals, puppies being one example
taken as written

explanation.surface: Puppies left out of doors make a mess, and here is the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here's' is a link word. A litter lout is the British term for someone who drops rubbish in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter lout is a person who drops rubbish carelessly, someone making a mess of public spaces.

clue.text: CD, say, almost entirely dreadful (American)

indicators.note: almost means the word for entirely loses its final letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in 'all alone'
bum is American slang for bad or worthless

explanation.surface: A disc that is nearly all dreadful, in the American way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL; BUM as an adjective meaning lousy is American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A CD is one example of an album, a collection of recorded tracks released together.

clue.text: Federation accepts core elements of some precepts

indicators.note: accepts means the federation word takes something inside it

parts.note: the Axis was the alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War

indicators.note: core elements of means the middle letters of the word some

explanation.surface: A federation takes on the central parts of certain principles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, a loose sense of 'federation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Axioms are self-evident principles or rules taken as given, much like precepts.

clue.text: Reduced fare for those boarding?

parts.note: the meal provided to lodgers, a fare for boarders, often shortened to its initials B and B

explanation.surface: A discount ticket for passengers getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced fare' suggests a cheap ticket and 'boarding' a train or plane; really the fare is food for lodgers, and 'reduced' hints at the familiar abbreviation B&B.
explanation.definitionFit: Guest houses offer overnight lodging with a morning meal, the fare given to people boarding there.

clue.text: Statesmen fiddling form of qualification

indicators.note: fiddling with something tampers with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians cheat on a qualifying form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges the letters of STATESMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test checks someone's income to decide whether they qualify for state help.

clue.text: A long time filling in Asian visa? That's novel

indicators.note: filling in means the long-time word goes inside the visa phrase

parts.note: a pass to India is permission to enter an Asian country
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A lengthy wait while completing an Asian visa form, which is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link; 'novel' looks like the adjective 'unusual', but it is the noun naming a book.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster's 1924 book about British India is a famous novel.

clue.text: Explorer having no end of a job with servant

indicators.note: no end of means the job word loses its final letter

parts.note: a task is a job
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: An explorer with an unfinished job and a manservant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' cuts TASK to TAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the Dutch explorer who sighted Tasmania and New Zealand.

clue.text: Most of sentence gets reduced in the end

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter of the sentence word

parts.note: a term is a prison sentence
minus means less, reduced by

explanation.surface: A prison term is mostly cut short in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims TERM to TER; 'gets' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is an end point, especially the last stop of a railway or bus line.

clue.text: The current thinking is to keep him occupied

definitions.text: The current thinking is to keep him occupied

parts.words: The current thinking is to keep him occupied
parts.note: read 'the current thinking' as the thoughts going on in someone's head right now: a telepath's business is exactly that

explanation.surface: Official policy is to keep a certain man busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current thinking' looks like prevailing opinion, but means the thoughts someone is having at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepathic person claims to perceive others' present thoughts, which is what occupies this performer.

clue.text: Pal limits cold feeling in fur

indicators.note: limits means the pal word surrounds and bounds the other piece

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
a chill is a cold feeling

explanation.surface: A friend restricts a cold feeling inside a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. China = mate comes from Cockney rhyming slang, china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent, prized as a luxury fur.

clue.text: Oddly stoical about expression of alternative medicine?

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the next piece
oddly means strangely, so the letters of stoical are jumbled

parts.note: or is the word expressing an alternative

explanation.surface: Strangely stoical about a form of alternative medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' also gives CASTOIL, the anagram of the seven letters. 'alternative medicine' reads as one phrase, but 'alternative' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor oil is a traditional laxative, long dosed out as a household medicine.

clue.text: Competent board dumping leader

indicators.note: dumping leader means the first letter of the board word is dropped

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A capable board gets rid of its chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping leader' removes T from TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable and skilled, a straight synonym of competent.

clue.text: Fight to secure it after picking up large dagger

indicators.note: to secure means the fight word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: picking up in a down clue means the word it is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out to grab something after a big pickup, involving a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' turns IT to TI, then L follows; 'to secure' puts the TIL inside SET-TO after its S. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Scottish writer regularly seen in Shanklin

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of Shanklin, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A Scottish author is often spotted in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link. Shanklin is a resort on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, a short-story writer of Scottish family.

clue.text: These days honest blokes will take time to make change

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era
just means fair and honest
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Nowadays decent men will take their time to make a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will take' and 'to make' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a small alteration or modification, a change made to something.

clue.text: Particular Schubert song turned up, receiving cheers

indicators.note: receiving means the song word takes in another piece
turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song, of which Schubert wrote hundreds
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A specific Schubert song makes a comeback, greeted with applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives DEIL from the song word. 'cheers' looks like applause but means thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is an individual item or particular, as in 'every particular of the case'.

clue.text: Loves to be seen here in a new car?

definitions.text: Loves to be seen here in a new car?

parts.words: Loves to be seen here in a new car?
parts.note: loves are zeros, as in tennis scores; a brand-new vehicle's mileage dial shows nothing but noughts

explanation.surface: People who love to be seen in a shiny new motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loves' reads as a verb about show-offs, but it is the noun: in tennis love means zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is the dashboard instrument counting distance travelled, all zeros in a fresh vehicle.

clue.text: Servant's dropping name by accident

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective meaning lucky, happening by chance

indicators.note: dropping means one letter of the servant word falls away

parts.note: a flunkey is a liveried manservant; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A servant drops someone's name by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes N from FLUNKEY. The definition is loose: it means 'happening by accident'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fluky comes about through a lucky chance rather than by design.

clue.text: Stop defending the old Lord after one's imprisoned

indicators.note: after means the lord abbreviation follows the other piece
imprisoned means the single letter is shut up inside the old word

parts.note: ye is the old form of the
I is the Roman numeral for one; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Stop protecting the old lord once someone is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop defending' together means give up, which is the definition; 'Stop' alone would leave 'defending' idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give up or surrender, to cease resisting or holding out.

clue.text: Call to stop which horses only acknowledge at first

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: A command to halt that horses alone respond to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' picks W, H, O and A from the four words in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the shouted command used to make a horse halt.

clue.text: A clear-cut decision — all one wants from a Customs official?

definitions.meaning: a matter so obvious it is settled at once

definitions.text: all one wants from a Customs official?
definitions.meaning: a traveller hopes the officer will just glance into the luggage and close it quickly

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: read literally, the phrase describes a suitcase being opened and promptly closed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a matter easily settled because the facts are obvious, and literally a suitcase briefly opened.

clue.text: Solid mix of metals has parts switched

indicators.note: has parts switched means the two halves of the metals word swap places

parts.note: an alloy is a mixture of metals

explanation.surface: A solid mixture of metals has had its components swapped around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has parts switched' swaps AL and LOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid supporter is a steadfast one, so solid here means faithful and dependable.

clue.text: Again assumed study requires work by Edward

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
op is short for opus, a work
Ted is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: A second look at the study needs a work by Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is a link word; 'by' places Edward's piece next to the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To readopt is to take up again, so readopted means assumed once more, as a role or name.
